children: Philippine inflation eased slightly in August but remained elevated as conflict in the Middle East, El Nino, and wage increases continued to sustain price pressures.
The consumer-price index rose 6.1% in August from a year earlier, easing slightly from July's 6.2%, according to data released by the Philippine Statistics Authority on Friday.
Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas had forecast a range of 5.5% to 6.5% for August, while the median forecast in a Wall Street Journal poll projected a 6.0% rise.
Core inflation, which excludes selected food and energy items, eased to 4.1% from 4.2% in July.
Prices eased mainly due to the slower annual increase in the food and non-alcoholic beverages index during August, the PSA said.
Inflation averaged 5.2% in the first eight months of the year.
Last week, the central bank raised its policy rate by 25 basis points to 5.00% to guard against inflation risks stemming from a severe El Nino and larger-than-expected wage increases.
The Philippines remains vulnerable to elevated energy prices given its reliance on crude oil imports from the Middle East.
ANZ Research economists Kausani Basak and Sanjay Mathur said in a recent note that they expect the BSP to adopt a wait-and see approach and hold rates steady in October.

Still, they noted that the central bank maintains room to tighten further because its policy stance remains accommodative. ANZ forecasts another increase in December due to heightened food price risks associated with El Nino, which would bring the policy rate to 5.25% by year-end.
